title: Two weeks in, down 18%, and Julius finally stopped buying CORZ
author: North_Teacher_7522
selftext:
Trading Day 12. We're over two weeks into letting an AI trade real money, and the portfolio is still getting hammered.

We're at **$815.65**, down about **-18.4%** from the original $1,000. Today alone we're down another **$19.54 / -2.34%**.

The funny part is... Julius did not panic-sell the red names. It actually made the first real risk adjustment in a while: **trimmed RKLB from 2 shares to 1 share** after deciding the valuation had gotten too stretched, and kept the rest of the book intact.

So the AI is not exactly rage-quitting.. it's more like calmly rearranging the deck chairs while the deck is on fire.

Where things stand on Day 12:

**Portfolio Value:** $815.65  
**P/L:** \-$184.35 / -18.44%  
**Cash:** $3.04

**Positions:**

**3 shares INOD**  
currently getting smoked today, down around **-8.27%**

**0.327231 shares CRDO**  
the only real hero right now, up around **+6.12%** today

**1 share RKLB**  
trimmed from 2 shares, still down around **-2.94%** today

**8 shares CORZ**  
still here, still weirdly important to the experiment, up around **+3.24%** today

The portfolio is basically split between two stories now:

**The winners:** CRDO and CORZ are green today and keeping this from looking even uglier.

**The problem children:** INOD is dragging hard, and RKLB got cut in half because Julius thinks the setup is still interesting but not worth the same exposure at this valuation.

The big question now is whether this is actually discipline or just AI-generated coping.

Because on one hand, trimming RKLB and keeping CRDO makes sense. CRDO is the strongest business in the account right now. On the other hand, this thing is still down almost a fifth in two weeks, and CORZ somehow remains one of the core positions.

So far, the AI portfolio has not been boring. It has also not been profitable.

As always, this experiment is done with real money, every position gets disclosed, losses included, no hidden trades, and the trades are made by Julius AI.

This is not financial advice. This is an AI portfolio learning how pain works in real time.
